erin_acme: Hey @support — hitting 401 invalid_api_key only in our release Android build pushed last night. Debug/dev builds are fine.

maria_support: Sorry for the trouble — can you paste the request log (headers) and which SDK + version youre using?

erin_acme: Using redwood-android 1.3.2, app v2.8.1 (release). Repro steps:
1) assembleRelease with minifyEnabled=true
2) open app and trigger API call
Observed request snippet from our okhttp logging: 
```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
Authorization: ApiKey sk_live_QWxABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP...TRUNCATED
Content-Type: application/json
```
Full key is injected at compile time via `buildConfigField` and is present in our CI env. Dev builds print the full key.

jon_mobile: Thanks — that looks like the release build/runtime is truncating the key. Are you injecting the key as a `buildConfigField` or a resource? Any 3rd-party R8/proguard string obfuscation plugins enabled?

erin_acme: We use `buildConfigField \"String\", \"REWOOD_API_KEY\", \\\"sk_live_QWxABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWX1234567890\\\"` in our app module gradle. We also added a 3rd-party \"string-obfuscator\" plugin to shrink/obfuscate literal strings in release builds.

maria_support: Can you confirm what actually ended up inside the APK? Two quick options:
- pull the release APK and grep classes.dex for the key (mask it before pasting)
- add a quick log right before the network send to dump `BuildConfig.REWOOD_API_KEY.length()` (mask output)

erin_acme: Pulled the APK and grepped classes.dex. The stored string inside the DEX shows `sk_live_QWxABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWX` (32 chars) but our original key is 47 chars. So its definitely being truncated in the release build. Disabling the string-obfuscator plugin restores the full key.

jon_mobile: Ok that pins it to the obfuscation step. That plugin is probably rewriting/shortening constant pools to save space. Two paths:
1) Disable that plugin for any secret-like constants (recommended).
2) Move the key out of compile-time constants and set it at runtime (secure remote config or CI-injected property at install time).

maria_support: For immediate unblock, disable the string-obfuscator and re-roll the release. Longer term we should make the SDK more defensive. Can you also run the app with env `REDWOOD_LOG=debug` and paste the masked Authorization header as it leaves the client? That will help confirm the exact truncation boundary.

erin_acme: Will do. We verified masked header: `ApiKey sk_live_QWxABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWX` (exactly 32 chars).

infra-bot: Ticket created RW-9876: android string-obfuscation plugin strips API key — assigned to jon_mobile.

jon_mobile: I'll add a defensive client-side check in the next SDK patch: validate prefix `sk_live_` and minimum length, and surface a clear error `Malformed API key: possible build-time obfuscation or truncation` with remediation steps (check R8/proguard plugins, avoid compile-time constants for secrets). ETA for PR: tomorrow.

erin_acme: Thanks — disabling the plugin fixed our immediate release. Please keep me posted on the SDK patch so we can flip obfuscation back on safely. :thumbsup:

maria_support: Thanks for the great repro, Erin. Filed notes for docs: add a short guide on \"Android builds that obfuscate literals can break API keys\" plus recommended rules (avoid buildConfig compile-time secrets, use runtime config).
